discriminating_terms: a suspicion that the meeting will finish earlier than planned
blind_attributions.rationale: The noun scopes over a neutral prediction about whether a future event will occur as expected. The meeting is not presented as a person suspected of misconduct (sense:001), and no target or information source is treated with general mistrust (sense:002); the clause is a tentative proposition, which is sense:003.

In “cast suspicion on” with a person as its complement, the clerk is made a possible wrongdoer, not merely someone whose account or reliability is distrusted. That person-directed accusation is sense:001; sense:002 would express mistrust of the clerk or the clerk’s information without casting the person as a suspect.

discriminating_terms: appeared at the corner of her mouth
blind_attributions.rationale: “A suspicion of a smile” is a barely perceptible trace of an expression appearing on the mouth. It is not a doubtful belief that someone smiled (sense:003) or distrust toward a person (sense:002); the faint manifestation is sense:004.

“With some suspicion” describes a wary, mistrustful attitude in the way the subject is received. No particular proposition is stated as a hunch (sense:003), and no person is accused of an offense (sense:001); the attitude is sense:002.

discriminating_terms: suspicion that the treasurer had committed fraud
blind_attributions.rationale: Although the suspicion is grammatically expressed with a that-clause, its content specifically casts the treasurer as the person who committed fraud. The headword therefore marks a person-directed allegation of wrongdoing (sense:001), unlike sense:003, where the uncertain proposition is not an accusation that a particular person committed an offense.

discriminating_terms: a strong suspicion that the delay was caused by a technical problem
blind_attributions.rationale: The suspicion is a strong but unconfirmed belief about the cause of a delay. The clause does not identify a person as a wrongdoer, which excludes sense:001, and the headword takes the cause proposition as its scope rather than describing generalized mistrust (sense:002); this is sense:003.

The construction “arrested on suspicion of” identifies the arrested people as suspected of committing the named offense. This is a person-directed criminal allegation (sense:001), not a tentative prediction or broad mistrust (senses:003 and :002).

“A suspicion of citrus” denotes a slight trace of citrus flavor in the sauce. This is a sensory degree reading (sense:004), not a doubtful proposition about citrus (sense:003) or distrust (sense:002).

“Came under suspicion” makes the employee the person regarded as a possible perpetrator after a disappearance. The frame places a person under an allegation of wrongdoing (sense:001); it is not merely a generalized attitude of distrust toward the employee (sense:002).

discriminating_terms: confirmed her suspicion that the battery was failing
blind_attributions.rationale: The suspicion is a tentative proposition about the battery’s condition, which subsequent results confirm. The battery is not a person accused of misconduct (sense:001), and the clause is a belief about a state rather than generalized distrust (sense:002); this is sense:003.

discriminating_terms: a suspicion of disappointment in his voice
blind_attributions.rationale: The phrase locates a faint trace of an emotion in the quality of the voice. It is not a proposition the speaker doubts (sense:003) or mistrust of a person or information (sense:002); the slight emotional manifestation is sense:004.

“Remained under suspicion” presents the contractor as a continuing possible wrongdoer whose suspected conduct is being checked. This is the status of a person under an allegation (sense:001), rather than mere doubt about the contractor’s general trustworthiness (sense:002).

discriminating_terms: the manager's suspicions that a guard had stolen the missing laptops
blind_attributions.rationale: The that-clause identifies a particular guard as the person who stole property, so the manager’s suspicion is an allegation that this person committed wrongdoing (sense:001). The fact that it is a proposition does not make it sense:003; that sense would cover an uncertain claim without this person-as-offender relation.

discriminating_terms: cast suspicion on the reliability of the company’s explanation
blind_attributions.rationale: The complement is the reliability of an explanation, so the headword expresses doubt about whether information is trustworthy. No person is alleged to have committed an offense (sense:001); this broad distrust of credibility is sense:002.

discriminating_terms: a sneaking suspicion that everyone already knew the answer
blind_attributions.rationale: The headword scopes over a tentative belief about what everyone knows. No one is alleged to have committed wrongdoing (sense:001), and the clause presents a hunch rather than an attitude of distrust toward information (sense:002); this is sense:003.

discriminating_terms: viewed the sudden policy change with suspicion
blind_attributions.rationale: “Viewed ... with suspicion” describes a wary, distrustful way of regarding something. It is not a specific tentative proposition (sense:003) or a person-directed accusation of wrongdoing (sense:001); this general mistrust is sense:002.

discriminating_terms: white with a suspicion of blue
blind_attributions.rationale: The phrase means the walls have a barely perceptible blue tint. Color as a slight sensory quality is sense:004, not a tentative belief about a proposition (sense:003) or mistrust (sense:002).
